files.README.md:
Node Express Starter

Quick start

1. Install dependencies:
   npm install

2. Start the server:
   npm start

   By default the server listens on port 3000. To change the port, set the PORT environment variable:
   PORT=8080 npm start

3. Visit http://localhost:3000/ in your browser.

Scripts

- npm start: run the Express server (node server.js)
- npm test: run a simple automated test that starts the server on a random port and POSTs /api/visit
- npm run build: copies public/ into dist/public and also copies server.js and package.json into dist/

Behavior & troubleshooting

- The app keeps an in-memory visit counter and attempts to persist the counter to visits.json in the project root. If the file is missing at startup the app begins at 0 and will create visits.json on the first write.
- If the server cannot write to disk (permissions, low-disk space), it will still increment in-memory and return success but with a warning flag in the JSON response.
- Frontend caches the last-known visit count in localStorage as a fallback for offline use.
- The simple test starts the server programmatically; if the default port is in use, the test chooses a random available port.

Requirements

- Node.js 14+ (LTS recommended)

Files of interest

- server.js: Express server and API endpoints
- public/: frontend assets (index.html, app.js, style.css)
- visits.json: created by the server when persisting counts (included in .gitignore)
